name: Inowon Sailing School compact solar network
subtitle: Minimal direct-DC Starlink and USB charging system

currency.note: Planning costs are in USD. Imported freight, duty, sales tax, and the Starlink service subscription are not included.

budget.note: The itemized planning estimate is $2,096.87 before freight, duty, tax, or subscription. The $2,350 working ceiling leaves about 12% for price movement and small omissions.

summary: Three lightweight 100 W Renogy panels form one series string feeding a Victron SmartSolar 100/20. Two locally purchased 12 V, 150 Ah deep-cycle batteries connect in parallel through independent 25 A positive breakers, so either battery can be isolated while the other keeps the system online. The controller's protected 20 A load output supplies only a regulated Starlink Mini branch and one 75 W USB-C/USB-A charging module; there is no inverter, separate router, shunt display, or PV combiner.

keyFacts.label: Solar array
keyFacts.detail: 3 × Renogy 100 W flexible panels in series · 62.1 Vmp · 73.2 V Voc

keyFacts.label: Battery bank
keyFacts.detail: 2 × 150 Ah deep-cycle batteries in parallel · independently isolated

keyFacts.label: Usable storage
keyFacts.detail: 50% planning depth of discharge · 0.9 kWh with one battery online

keyFacts.label: Planning load
keyFacts.detail: 8 h Starlink plus one laptop and two phone charges · includes conversion reserve

keyFacts.label: Imported shipment
keyFacts.detail: About 24.7 kg packed · only batteries and both 4 mm² cable lots purchased in Chuuk

powerModel.assumptions: The energy budget uses the documented upper end of Starlink Mini average consumption (40 W for 8 hours), one 70 Wh laptop charge, two 15 Wh phone charges, and 100 Wh/day for DC conversion loss, controller consumption, cable loss, and operating reserve. Solar yield uses 300 W × 4.0 peak-sun-hours × 75%. The simultaneous design case is 60 W maximum Starlink input plus up to 78 W input to the 75 W USB module and converter overhead, rounded to 150 W. At the 11.8 V load-disconnect floor this is about 12.7 A, below the SmartSolar 100/20 load output's 20 A rating. Site shading, actual Starlink hours, laptop battery size, battery chemistry, and local weather remain unverified.

shipping.note: Imported weight is a planning sum of item and package estimates. Only the batteries and both 4 mm² cable lots are excluded from the imported shipment and purchased in Chuuk; the battery boxes are imported. Verify every packed carton before booking freight.

bom.item: Renogy RNG-100DB-H-US 100 W flexible solar panel
bom.description: Three modules wired as one 3S string: 300 W, 62.1 Vmp, 73.2 V Voc, 4.84 A Imp and 5.16 A Isc. Manufacturer dimensions are 1093 × 582 × 3 mm and 2.4 kg each. The official store listed $149.99 and backordered on 3 Sep 2026; confirm stock or approve an electrically compatible substitute before ordering.
bom.weightNote: Manufacturer net panel weight; packing is covered by the shipment allowance.

bom.item: Victron SmartSolar MPPT 100/20 · SCC110020160R
bom.description: Compact 100 V / 20 A controller with Bluetooth and a 20 A load output. The 300 W array is 10 W above its 290 W nominal 12 V PV rating, so only a small STC peak can clip; the controller is specified to limit input power. Configure the exact local lead-acid profile and BatteryLife load disconnect before service.

bom.item: Starlink Mini Kit
bom.description: The Mini includes its own Wi-Fi, so this design omits a separate router. Starlink specifies 25–40 W average, 12–48 V / 60 W input, and a 15 m DC cable. The allowance uses the current Micronesia hardware starting price of $260 and excludes service; the official Micronesia Roam page currently lists service from $50/month. Remove this row if Inowon already owns a compatible transferable kit.
bom.weightNote: Planning packed-kit estimate; the published dish, kickstand and 15 m cable assembly is 1.53 kg.

bom.item: Starlink Mini 12 V to regulated 24 V step-up adapter · 72 W
bom.description: Retains the original Pasana design's regulated Starlink branch while avoiding an inverter. The planning unit accepts roughly 9–20 V and outputs 24 V / 72 W. Bench-test startup at the low-voltage disconnect point with the complete Starlink cable; do not rely on an unregulated 12 V long run.
bom.weightNote: Planning allowance for converter, switch and leads; verify received package.

bom.item: Coolgear ChargeIT! Mini 75 W USB-C + USB-A module · CG-PD60PPS
bom.description: One hard-wired module replaces cigarette-lighter sockets and splitters. It provides up to 60 W USB-C PD for a laptop plus 18 W USB-A, with 75 W nominal / 78 W peak combined output. Confirm that the supplied input connector accepts the selected 4 mm² conductor or use the included short pigtail with an enclosed listed splice.

bom.item: 10 A common-trip two-pole PV disconnect breaker · 100 VDC minimum
bom.description: Disconnects both ungrounded PV conductors. The 10 A rating is above 1.25 × the 5.16 A string Isc and below the panel's 15 A maximum series-fuse rating. Select a genuine common-trip DC device with at least 100 VDC working voltage and a documented interrupt rating.

bom.item: 25 A battery-positive isolation breakers
bom.description: One resettable breaker on each battery positive, mounted shortest-practical to its terminal. Equal-length positive and negative 4 mm² leads connect each battery to the common buses. Either branch can carry the entire 20 A load-output limit while the other battery is isolated.

bom.item: 25 A SmartSolar battery-side breaker
bom.description: Protects and isolates the controller battery connection. Victron specifies a 25–30 A battery fuse range for the SmartSolar 100/20; this design uses the lower 25 A value to coordinate with short 4 mm² conductors.

bom.item: 10 A Starlink and USB branch breakers
bom.description: One resettable 10 A breaker per load branch. Their combined possible rating equals the SmartSolar load output's documented 20 A continuous limit; the modeled simultaneous demand is about 150 W / 12.7 A at the 11.8 V disconnect floor.

bom.item: Covered positive and negative busbars · 60 A minimum
bom.description: Small covered buses provide balanced battery landings and one controller branch without stacking multiple lugs on battery posts. Select corrosion-resistant hardware with at least six usable landings across the pair.

bom.item: Ventilated corrosion-resistant equipment enclosure · about 600 × 500 × 180 mm
bom.description: One indoor or deeply sheltered enclosure contains the MPPT, busbars and breakers while preserving terminal guarding and the controller's ventilation clearance. The 600 × 500 × 180 mm planning envelope is represented at scale in the 3D view. It is not a sealed box: use screened high/low vents and keep salt spray, insects, and battery gas out. Final size still requires a full-scale hardware layout.
bom.weightNote: Planning estimate for enclosure, backplate and vent hardware.

bom.item: DIN rail, terminal covers, cable glands, and enclosure hardware
bom.description: Small installation lot for secure mounting, finger-safe terminal covers, strain relief, labels, and screened enclosure entries.

bom.item: Genuine-compatible MC4-to-bare PV pigtail pair
bom.description: Factory-terminated pigtails connect the outer ends of the three-panel series string to locally purchased 4 mm² PV cable without requiring field-crimped solar connectors. Verify polarity before mating.

bom.item: Weatherproof Starlink cable entry and strain relief
bom.description: Maintains bend radius, strain relief and weather sealing where the OEM cable enters the building. Do not substitute an ordinary exposed barrel splice outdoors.

bom.item: 4 mm² copper lugs, ferrules, enclosed splices, labels, and heat-shrink
bom.description: Corrosion-resistant terminations for the selected battery posts, breakers, buses, MPPT and load pigtails. Battery lug hole size cannot be finalized until the exact Chuuk battery model is known.

bom.item: Flexible-panel mounting and edge-restraint kit
bom.description: Provisional allowance for manufacturer-compatible adhesive, mechanical perimeter restraint, cable clips and corrosion-resistant fasteners. Final attachment and wind design require the Polowat roof material, dimensions and exposure; never rely on adhesive alone in severe wind and never walk on the flexible modules.
bom.weightNote: Provisional mounting-kit allowance pending roof survey.

bom.item: USB-C laptop cable and phone charging leads
bom.description: One e-marked 100 W-capable USB-C cable for the laptop plus common phone leads. Actual laptop charge rate is limited to 60 W by the selected module.

bom.item: 12 V 150 Ah deep-cycle lead-acid batteries · matched pair
bom.description: Buy two identical batteries of the same chemistry, model, date code and state of charge. The planning model assumes 12 V / 150 Ah each, 42 kg each and 50% usable depth of discharge. Flooded, AGM and GEL products require different charge settings and ventilation; do not commission until the exact label and datasheet are recorded.
bom.weightNote: Typical planning mass for a 150 Ah lead-acid deep-cycle battery; replace with the selected Chuuk product value.

bom.item: 4 mm² UV-resistant PV cable · red and black
bom.description: Ten metres each of red and black PV-rated copper conductor for a provisional 10 m one-way array home run. The 3S string carries only 4.84 A nominal, keeping voltage drop small. Replace this quantity after measuring the actual roof-to-controller route.

bom.item: 4 mm² flexible DC cable · red and black
bom.description: Single selected size for short battery, controller and load-distribution runs. Make both battery positive leads equal to each other and both negative leads equal to each other; keep every high-current run shortest-practical. The 25 A upstream protection is provisional until hot-installation ampacity and the received conductor markings are verified.

bom.item: Corrosion-resistant battery boxes, covers, and restraints
bom.description: Each battery requires individual retention, terminal guarding and chemistry-appropriate ventilation. Keep electronics out of the battery-gas path and protect against salt water and conductive debris.
bom.weightNote: Planning mass for two boxes and restraints.

operatingRules: Use the Starlink Mini's integrated Wi-Fi; do not add a separate router or inverter unless the load model is redesigned.

Keep the Starlink account and service plan valid for stationary use in Micronesia. The hardware budget excludes recurring service; current advertised Micronesia service starts at $50/month and must be confirmed at the exact Polowat address.

Keep both batteries online only when they are the same chemistry, model, age and state of charge. To remove a failed battery, open its 25 A positive breaker before touching any terminal; the other battery can carry the complete 20 A controller load-output limit.
Give Starlink priority during low-energy periods. Stop laptop charging first if the controller enters BatteryLife load shedding or if repeated low-voltage disconnects occur.
Keep all three series panels unshaded. Shade on one module constrains the whole string; clean salt and debris with water and a non-abrasive sponge, and never walk on a flexible panel.
The system has no AC output. Do not connect an inverter, power tools, pumps, refrigerators or other unmodeled loads to the battery buses or controller load output.
Keep the equipment enclosure dry, ventilated and outside the battery-gas path. Preserve terminal covers, cable strain relief and the Starlink weather seal.
commissioning: Record the exact battery manufacturer, model, chemistry, charge voltages, terminal style, weight and purchase price. Charge both batteries separately to the same rested voltage before first paralleling them.

Confirm every breaker is genuinely DC rated for its location, verify interrupt capacity against the selected batteries, and verify 4 mm² conductor ampacity in the actual hot/bundled installation before energizing.

Connect in Victron's required order: battery first, confirm detected 12 V system, connect loads, then close the PV disconnect. Set the manufacturer-specific lead-acid charge profile and disable automatic equalization unless the battery datasheet explicitly requires it.
Configure the SmartSolar load output to BatteryLife or an installer-approved low-voltage threshold. Confirm that both Starlink and USB branches shut down and recover cleanly without chattering.
Bench-test the regulated Starlink branch with the full OEM cable at the 11.8 V planning floor. Measure cold-start current, average draw and converter temperature for at least two hours.
Test battery A alone, battery B alone and both together. In each state, run Starlink and a 60 W laptop charge simultaneously and verify breaker temperature, bus voltage and connector voltage drop.
Measure the final PV home run and battery/enclosure spacing before cutting cable. Recalculate voltage drop if the array is more than 10 m one way from the controller.
Have the Polowat installer approve panel attachment for the actual roof and wind exposure, then photograph labels, torque marks, breaker positions and finished cable routing for the handoff.
